import math

def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    # Prefix sums S[i] is sum of a[0...i-1]
    S = [0] * (n + 1)
    current = 0
    for i in range(n):
        current += a[i]
        S[i+1] = current
        
    # Lower convex hull of points (index, S[index])
    # Stores indices of points on the hull
    hull = []
    
    # Initialize best average with the first valid subarray a[0...k-1]
    # Sum S[k], length k
    best_p = S[k]
    best_q = k
    
    # Iterate j from k to n
    # j is the exclusive end index of the subarray
    for j in range(k, n + 1):
        # The new candidate start index is j - k
        i_new = j - k
        
        # Add i_new to hull, maintaining lower convex hull property
        # Points are (idx, S[idx]). We want the lower hull, so slopes between consecutive vertices must be increasing.
        # If adding i_new makes the slope decrease (or stay same), the last vertex is redundant.
        while len(hull) >= 2:
            i2 = hull[-1]
            i1 = hull[-2]
            
            # Slope 1: (S[i2] - S[i1]) / (i2 - i1)
            # Slope 2: (S[i_new] - S[i2]) / (i_new - i2)
            # Check if Slope 1 >= Slope 2
            # Using cross multiplication to avoid floats
            # (S[i2] - S[i1]) * (i_new - i2) >= (S[i_new] - S[i2]) * (i2 - i1)
            
            val1 = (S[i2] - S[i1]) * (i_new - i2)
            val2 = (S[i_new] - S[i2]) * (i2 - i1)
            
            if val1 >= val2:
                hull.pop()
            else:
                break
        hull.append(i_new)
        
        # Find i in hull that maximizes the average (S[j] - S[i]) / (j - i)
        # The function f(i) = (S[j] - S[i]) / (j - i) is unimodal on the vertices of the lower convex hull.
        # We use ternary search to find the maximum.
        
        low = 0
        high = len(hull) - 1
        
        while high - low > 2:
            m1 = low + (high - low) // 3
            m2 = high - (high - low) // 3
            
            idx1 = hull[m1]
            idx2 = hull[m2]
            
            # Compare f(idx1) and f(idx2)
            # f(idx) = (S[j] - S[idx]) / (j - idx)
            # f(idx1) < f(idx2) <=> (S[j] - S[idx1]) * (j - idx2) < (S[j] - S[idx2]) * (j - idx1)
            
            lhs = (S[j] - S[idx1]) * (j - idx2)
            rhs = (S[j] - S[idx2]) * (j - idx1)
            
            if lhs < rhs:
                low = m1
            else:
                high = m2
        
        # Linear scan in the small remaining range [low, high] to find the best i
        best_local_i = hull[low]
        
        for idx in range(low, high + 1):
            i = hull[idx]
            # Compare current i with best_local_i
            # We want to see if (S[j] - S[i]) / (j - i) > (S[j] - S[best_local_i]) / (j - best_local_i)
            # Cross multiply:
            num_curr = S[j] - S[i]
            den_curr = j - i
            num_best = S[j] - S[best_local_i]
            den_best = j - best_local_i
            
            if num_curr * den_best > num_best * den_curr:
                best_local_i = i
        
        # Update global best
        num = S[j] - S[best_local_i]
        den = j - best_local_i
        
        # Compare with global best
        if num * best_q > best_p * den:
            best_p = num
            best_q = den

    # Simplify the fraction
    common = math.gcd(best_p, best_q)
    return [best_p // common, best_q // common]
